svg.aria-label: How to write ्: one unbroken stroke · 1 movement
svg.title: Writing ्
svg.desc: 1 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ् (devanagari), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansDevanagari-Static.ttf. Stroke order after HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0, Devanagari recognizer, class 61 (्, virama): stored online-handwriting prototypes from native writers (MIT licence, 2012) <https://lipitk.sourceforge.net/lipi-reco.htm>. Source note on variation: The recognizer stores native writers' tablet pen traces, each resampled to 60 points. 80 of the 82 stored prototypes of the virama (98%) are one pen-down stroke, and 79 of the 82 move downward, starting at the top. Because the traces are stretched to a square, they cannot show the slant; the slant is the printed one, so the stroke runs down to the right. Each sign was written by itself, with no consonant beside it, so the traces fix the sign's own strokes but not when it is written against its consonant or the headline; the book draws the sign alone and composes no Devanagari word from it. The traces are scaled to a square, so they fix the start, the direction and the pen lifts, not the proportions: the path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Devanagari outline of the sign on its own. The underlying HP Labs data is licensed for research use only, so only counts and shares are cited here, and no trace was copied. Handwriting varies by writer.
